target_customer: Salaried and underbanked individuals and agents in Nigeria who need loans and payments
problem: Many Nigerians lack access to formal credit and banking; lenders cannot underwrite people without credit files cheaply.
business_model: Digital lender earning interest and fees, expanded into payments and banking

founders.name: Wale Akanbi
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder and CTO in Techpoint coverage; not listed on the YC page.

competitors.name: Kiakia
competitors.what: Nigerian credit scoring and peer to peer lending platform
competitors.traction_then: Public launch in November 2016 per its co-founder

technical_complexity.rationale: Credit scoring with local bureau integration and payments integration, standard fintech engineering with some underwriting difficulty.

defensibility.rationale: Repayment data on employed borrowers helps underwriting, but many digital lenders served the same market.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Banks did not stop digital lenders; Aella later bought Flourish Microfinance Bank and became a licensed bank in 2024.

market_need_then: Nigeria had a large underbanked population and few digital lenders in 2017.

identity.logo: new logo introduced with the 2024 rebrand; not described in sources
identity.voice_and_tone: Bank The AELLA Way tagline on its site

rebrands.why: Followed acquisition of Flourish Microfinance Bank to offer banking services, per founder

brand_strength.rationale: Regional press coverage of funding and the rebrand; no evidence of strong community or viral brand assets.

pivots.to: Full stack fintech with payments, then microfinance bank
pivots.why: Company said it would expand into payments with the debt financing; rebranded in 2024 after buying a bank

outcome_analysis: Aella grew from a Nigerian digital lender into a payments platform and, in 2024, a licensed microfinance bank after buying Flourish MFB. Funding found is a small 2017 seed and a $10M debt line in 2020, so growth appears to have been financed largely by debt and revenue. It is still operating with about 60 staff and claims over 2 million users.
notes: Some outlets call the 2017 raise $2M seed; the opened Disrupt Africa article says undisclosed, so the amount is null. The 2020 $10M debt round is reported by many outlets (Techpoint, TechCabal, Nairametrics, Disrupt Africa). Founders' backgrounds not found in an opened source. Only one competitor had a source dated near the batch.
